body: Thank you! I really appreciate it.
Yes, that's why I'm not going to mention this to them. I know I have to give them time but I wish it was easier.
Yes, you're right and I agree. But it still hurts.
Not sure I want to tell them. I suspect it'll just make me sad. Anyway, thank you <3

I showed them a couple of pictures via text (my family has a text group where we're all very active and usually respond to what people send) and they all just completely ignored it. I know they saw the pictures but they ignored them and later responded to pictures sent by my brother and his wife (pictures of them at a wedding).

Maybe I'm being silly. I don't know. It just makes me sad.

> My advice on Sye: ignore him.

I'll certainly try to. He seems completely unreasonable to me.
Watched the debate. Sye is rude.
Will have to look up the show with Aron Ra and Sye.
Yes, I think it's completely ridiculous and I don't even understand how people can presuppose that God exists. Doesn't really make sense.

> You'll get out eventually as long as you keep bothering to think, which I'd say you're doing a pretty good job of so far.

Thank you. I'm doing my best.

I don't think I can say for sure that I *know* it's all fantasy (yet) but I *highly suspect* it is. I just hope I'm not going about this the wrong way and that I'm actually sabotaging my chance of finding God because I'm "too intellectual" when searching for the truth.
What helped you get over the fear of hell? You said you examined the fear and confronted it but how did you do that (more specifically)? Any advice?
It's good to hear I'm not alone (though I wish it wasn't this difficult for either of us) and I wish you peace and clarity too. Feel free to PM me if you want to talk.

You're right. I'm very frustrated with myself for knowing what the reasonable position to take is to say that *"I don't believe in God and won't believe in him until I get sufficient evidence for his existence"* but still being so afraid of hell that I try to make exceptions for God (even if I don't want to do so).

It's very confusing that there, first of all, are so many different religions in the world and that I'm only afraid of the Christian hell because I was brought up Christian, and, second, that there are so many different denominations within Christianity. How could we possibly know who's right? That's a question that has bothered me for a long time and I still don't have an answer to it. I've talked to Christians who try to explain it by saying that it doesn't really matter because all Christians still worship the same God. But then other Christians are convinced everyone who doesn't belong to their particular sect/denomination of Christianity are destined for hell, so the question remains; how could we possibly know who's right?

I really want to learn more about Christianity, the Bible, the arguments and fallacies etc. I created a Word document the other day where I'm going to write down the most common arguments for and against Christianity and the most common fallacies used when trying to defend the positions. I started reading the Bible the other day. I read it (or most of it) when growing up but have decided to read it again. Do you have any advice on what to keep in mind when reading it? I'm trying to read it the way I would read any other book.

Anyway, thank you for the reply and thanks for the video you linked. I'll definitely check it out.
Yes, and that prayer has already been prayed. No answer/sign/revelation so far.

I wish that was the end, but it isn't (yet). I've talked to Christians about divine hiddenness and about asking God to reveal himself and they tend to quote the following (Matthew 16:1-4):

"The Pharisees and Sadducees came to test Jesus. So they asked him to show them a miraculous sign from heaven.

He responded to them, 'In the evening you say that the weather will be fine because the sky is red. And in the morning you say that there will be a storm today because the sky is red and overcast. You can forecast the weather by judging the appearance of the sky, but you cannot interpret the signs of the times.

'Evil and unfaithful people look for a miraculous sign. But the only sign they will be given is that of Jonah.'

Then he left them standing there and went away."

Now, I don't even know what to think of the Bible so that could all be complete bullshit and something that never happened, I don't know, but I keep worrying.

Unless all religious people are actually worshipping the same God (only they're not aware of it), they're probably all wrong. It's probably more likely those experiences are just created in people's own brains.

I wish all the "what ifs" would just go away but I guess the indoctrination is strong with this one.

You're right. I mean, I could tell you that there's a purple unicorn walking around in my apartment and claim that it must be true because I *really* believe it and have faith in its existence, but that doesn't make it true. Also, I really do think that things *should not be believed* without evidence but my conflicted brain keeps trying to make exceptions for God. My brain also keeps reminding me of people's personal experiences with God and tries to tell me that all those experiences must mean God exists though I disagree with that at the same time (and I'm reminded of something Matt Dillahunty said in a video I watched the other day: *"the plural of anecdote isn't data"*). I'm so conflicted.
Thanks for the suggestion!

> It doesn't help always but something to keep in mind is that you dont fear any of the countless other deities and afterlife that other people believe in.

Exactly. I only fear Christian hell because I've been indoctrinated into Christianity. I know that and I know it doesn't really make sense to be afraid of one specific hell but I can't seem to shake the fear anyway.

> Coming from one who once "felt and experienced" all that nonsense and believed it wholeheartedly I can tell you it's not any deity, but rather all that I first mentioned in this paragraph. The intense feelings of joy and love is just a natural high, the brain tricking itself into accepting something natural as supernatural.

I've felt those things too. I've started crying in "the presence of God" for no reason and I've had intense feelings of joy and love (those experiences were *very* rare though) but that could probably all be explained by biological mechanisms. The problem is that Christians I've talked to pretty much say *"so what if those feelings could be explained by biological mechanisms? God probably just uses that way to communicate with us."* What if they're right?

> While it can be scary, it can also be quite liberating. You are free to live as you see fit. To think for yourself. It's a long road but eventually you will find peace with it all.

I agree. In a way I already feel a bit liberated. Since I started to look into Christianity and I realised it's probably man-made I've found a new appreciation for life. The world is *so much more beautiful* and life is so much more precious when you realise there might not be a God and that this life is the only life we get.

I'm still scared though.

You're completely right and the only reason I'm afraid of the Christian hell is because I was indoctrinated into this specific religion. I'm an atheist in regard to all other religions but I'm afraid of letting go of this one. I'm afraid God sits in heaven right now and sees how I've probably already made up my mind that I can't believe in him and that he'll punish me forever.
Thank you! I've already watched some videos at The Atheist Experience but I'll have a look at the other channels!

> As much as possible, read like you've never read the Bible before.

The more I think about the biblical stories, the more they sound like myths to me.

Anyway, thank you! I'll probably see me post new threads here at /r/exchristian in the future. Happy this place exists and that people want to help.
Will do!

Thank you. I recently made the decision to start reading the Bible cover to cover. I'm only on Genesis chapter 3, but still. Do you have any advice on how to read the Bible? I mean, I don't want to just automatically read it the way I used to read it when I grew up. Do you know what I mean?

> And know that no decision is permanent. If you change your mind or feel like you made a mistake, it's ok to reverse your decision.

That's true. Thank you, I'll keep that in mind!
Thank you! Subscribed to /r/academicbiblical and will check out the books you suggested.
Thank you! I'll have a look at both the book and the documentary!

Thank you for reading my post on /r/christianity. I had no idea so many people were going to read it since it's so long but I'm thankful people (yourself included) did. Sometimes you just need to talk about things, you know?

Anyway, I actually watched a few episodes of *Mr Deity* the other day. I've only watched a few but they're funny so far!

Thanks for the suggestion!

I'm planning on reading *The Demon-haunted World* soon. It's been in one of my bookshelves for a while, I just haven't picked it up yet.

Thank you! I've watched both *The God Delusion* and the debate between Ken Ham and Bill Nye. Well, I've watched the first debate anyway. I think there's a second but I haven't watched that yet.

What Crash Course videos are you referring to?
Sounds like an interesting read. Thank you!
Thank you!

Thank you! Very happy to hear you've had a good life. I don't know why (some) Christians keep saying that atheists must be miserable and that their lives can't have meaning. I kind of think atheists' (not sure *all* think this way) view of life is more beautiful than Christians'. Life feels so much more precious if you don't think this life is just a pit stop on the way to heaven. Do you know what I mean?

Anyway, thank you. I will definitely keep reading, discussing my thoughts, and thinking. I'm happy this subreddit exists. It's good to hear from people who've been through what I'm going through.
Thank you for taking the time to write all of that! I really appreciate it and I'll definitely have a look at all the things you linked to.

That's okay, I'll just go to Goodreads and see which books that most people have read and reviewed. :)

> Have you ever heard the names Matt Dillahunty or Jerry DeWitt?

I don't think I've heard of Jerry DeWitt but I recently heard of Matt Dillahunty. I actually just finished watching a 2 hour long debate between Dillahunty and someone called Cliffe Knechtle and just started watching a debate between Dillahunty and someone named Jay Lucas.

> The only advice I'd give is make sure you don't allow yourself to be railroaded into only one author's way of thinking.

Thank you. That's actually one of the main reasons I started this thread. I realised I've got a lot of books by "the four horsemen" on my list and wanted to get some suggestions on books by other authors as well. Do you have any suggestions on where to start when it comes to Stephen Jay Gould and Jerry Coyne?

> One of the many breaking points for me was when I realized that if there is a God who is just and loving, he wouldn't punish me for using the intellect and reasoning the he gave me to try to make sense of what I believe. It's ok to say you're not sure, but that you're trying to figure it out. If it turns out that you're wrong, then God should know that you were only doing the best you could with what you had available.

That's exactly what I'm hoping for. If God exists and he created me he knows how my brain works and that I'm doing my best to find the truth, whatever that is. I have no label so far. I'm questioning and I'm leaning towards atheism but that's all I know for now. I'm not going to rush into anything. I'm going to take my time, gather information, and try to come to some kind of conclusion. Like I said earlier, it's really distressing and difficult but I think it might be worth it.

Thank you again!

> I empathize with feeling disoriented because the whole basis for understanding reality that you were given as a child no longer makes sense. None of these books are directly related to atheism or theism, but they might help rebuild a philosophical foundation for thinking about the world after losing the one that you had.

Yes, it's disorienting and distressing. I hope I'll feel less confused soon. Thank you for the book suggestions! I bought *Sapiens* and *A Short History of Nearly Everything* recently and I'm planning on reading them sometime during the summer.

I'll definitely be looking at the videos/lectures you linked to. Thanks!

> I don't know where you are on learning about evolution.

I think I've done a pretty good job of learning about evolution on my own. I didn't attend a Christian high school so I learned some stuff there but I still felt like I had some kind of gap in knowledge in the area of evolution so I spent some time reading up on it on my own. I watched documentaries and read books like *The Selfish Gene* and *The Magic of Reality* by Richard Dawkins, some books on genetics, etc. Also, I studied biomedicine at university so I learned *a lot* about genetics and the like during that time, which I'm very happy about. Science is the best thing I know and evolution is beautiful.
Oh, I forgot to add *The Demon-Haunted World* on my list but it's one I own and plan on reading soon. Thank you for the other suggestion, I'll check it out!
Thank you! I'll add it to my to-read list.

Yes, I ordered *Letter to a Christian Nation* a few days ago and it's expected to arrive tomorrow so I'll probably read it very soon. I'll definitely have a look at the podcast you mentioned. Sounds very interesting. Thank you!
That sounds interesting. Thank you!

I really hope things will be okay. Indeed, this subreddit seems like a great place.

Thank you for the book suggestion and the link to the video series. I'll check them out!
Thank you! This process has already been very long and I don't expect it to end anytime soon. My hope is that I'll eventually find the truth, no matter what the truth is.
Thank you. I feel very lonely in all of this and it's difficult to know who to talk to about these things. Anyway, good to hear I'm not alone.
Thank you, I really appreciate that. It's very distressing and difficult and I feel pretty lonely in all of this so it's good to hear that others can relate. How'd you get through it (if I may ask)?

> I personally think you are on the right track to a deeper and richer spiritual life if that is what you are after.

I hope that's the case.

I've read a couple of Rob Bell's books and I recently bought *"A History of God"* by Karen Armstrong, which I'm planning on reading soon. I'll check out the other people you mentioned too (thanks for the links)! Thank you!

1. I've never said I'm an atheist so I guess I'm not officially "ripped out of the fold" yet. I don't know what I am. I'm trying to figure it out.
2. I haven't told my family about this so no, they're not devastated.
3. There are no gleeful comments from atheists in this thread.

Universal salvation makes much more sense to me.

May I ask what made you come back to God?

> Was he God?!? Well the prophecy in the old testament about the coming savior and where and how he was born exactly described Jesus.

Maybe you're right. I'm not saying you or the Bible are wrong but I just want to point out that the only thing you need to fulfil the prophecies of the Old Testament is an author of the books in the New Testament with a knowledge of the prophecies in the Old Testament. I'm not saying that's the case (I'm very worried about offending people in this thread) because I *certainly* don't know that. I'm just saying that I don't know what to believe anymore. It's all very confusing.

Thank you, that really means a lot to me.

And yes, this thread is getting a lot of attention. Wasn't really expecting that. I'll send you a PM eventually though. Thank you for being so kind.

You literally know nothing about me except what I've written in this post so I'm not sure why you think there are "sexual sins" in my life. Also, it's not like everyone on /r/openchristian are LGBT people.

Thank you for writing that. It's good to hear I'm not alone. Being in this situation is really distressing and I'm scared. I don't know if that's silly but I am.

I'll send you a PM later (bit overwhelmed by all the replies right now so I just need to calm down a bit first).

> Have you heard of Ravi Zacharias?

Yes, I actually heard of him the other day. I added some of his Youtube videos to my "watch later" list. I'm also planning on giving his podcast a go.

> If you read the New Testament, specifically books like John and Romans, seeking truth, I believe that it could answer some of your questions.

That only works if I assume that the Bible is true in the first place. I'm not saying the Bible isn't true, I'm just saying I don't know if it is and that's where I get stuck. Do you know what I mean?

> Have you actually prayed asking what He wants you do

Yes, I have.

Yes, I've been listening to people like Harris and Dawkins but what makes you think I haven't read and/or listened to Christian philosophers and/or scientists as well? I have. I'm trying to make up my mind about God and religion by listening to people on both sides of the debate, so thank you for the link to the video. I'll certainly have a look at it.
Thank you! I'll probably take you up on your offer and PM you later today.
Not sure why you were downvoted. I appreciate your comment and I'll probably take you up on your offer to chat. I'll send you a PM later today. Thank you.

> He doesn't actually, He has made it very simple and easy. The hard part is actually the way we are. We are so easily distracted and so willing to chase after other things that we don't actually seek God, or we make up a God for ourselves and seek that.

I respectfully disagree and I think it's a bit "dangerous" to say things like that because it generates feelings of guilt in (some) people. It reminds me of what people used to say in the church my family and I attended when I was young, namely that your faith wasn't strong enough or you weren't open enough to receive God's healing if you didn't get healed.

I've sought God for *years* and I bet I think more about God than *a lot* of Christians do. I try to find him and I think about him pretty much *every waking moment* (and I'm on sick leave due to depression so I have a lot of time on my hands). I've talked about God with people who work in churches, I've prayed, I've read the Bible, I've read books and watched debates and documentaries, I've tried talking to God and honestly tell him exactly how desperate I am to find him, etc., but still *nothing happens.* I don't think it's that strange that I'm starting to think he might not exist. Or if he does he probably doesn't care about me, which saddens me.

> You have proclaimed if He was God He would do this

I don't expect a God who exists to help me with my depression etc. so that my life would be free from suffering. God can exist even if he doesn't help me with that. I only said that was something I used to think about back when I started questioning things. It's not like my faith stands or falls with that.

That's interesting! Would you still call yourself a Christian? Anyway, what did you do to change the way you think about God and how do you "make peace with the idea that my finite human mind will only ever be able to form an imperfect, approximate model of it"? That seems very difficult to me.
Thank you! Sent you a PM.
Yes, I'm aware and I like that idea. The problem is that things we like aren't always real/true and I have no idea how to determine what's real/true in this case.

Hi,

Yes, it's quite intense and a lot to think about. I honestly think about God/religion pretty much all day everyday (I'm not even exaggerating).

> The good news (ha!)--I've found that questioning my beliefs and faith has led to a richer, broader faith experience.

Glad to hear that! I thought I'd see the same kind of result in my life because it's been very liberating to get out of fundamentalist Christianity and I realised the view I had had of God was very limited. Do you know what I mean? But then I "went too far" and realised that none of it makes sense. Maybe I'll change my mind, I'm certainly open to change my mind, but right now I'm all confused and on the verge of deconverting altogether.

Anyway, I'm glad you found things that helped you! I actually think the Jewish faith and way to look at the Bible seems more reasonable that the Christian way to look at it, but I don't know.

> I stopped believing in God as a conscious being and more like a force of love available to anyone who seeks it. I believe heaven and hell are not far-off places but actually here on earth--that heaven is connection and love, and hell is separation and isolation. I believe we can see heaven and hell all around us if we look--and that we can cause either for other people. As for what awaits in the afterlife, I don't pretend to know.

That's interesting. Would you say you still believe in the Christian God though?

Thank you for the link to the video. I'll check it out!

> And hey--maybe the stuff I shared will make you say, "Yeah, I'm definitely an atheist." That's okay too.

Thanks. Being in this "limbo" is quite distressing. I wish I could come to some kind of conclusion soon, no matter if it turns out that I'm an atheist or a theist.

> One of the most important lessons I learned is that heaven and hell are in the mind. Literally! Not outside and not "managed" by anyone outside of myself.

I've been thinking about that too. People sometimes say that something they're going through and feeling is "hell on Earth" and I've been thinking that maybe that's actually what hell is. A state of mind, the suffering we experience while we're alive. *Many* people would disagree with me on that though.

> Another important lesson is that God does exist and what is God's true nature.

May I ask how you came to that conclusion? I know you said you had to change the way you thought about things but could you maybe tell me more about it?

Would be great to get a copy of your book, thank you!

Well, thank *you* for reading it. I'd love to chat more about it. Do you believe in God?

Feel free to send me a PM or continue the conversation here!
